title: Passive losses and AMT planning — Leah Nakamura
instructions: Leah Nakamura, single, asks for help with her 2025 return and planning. Compute the amounts and answer the planning questions.

exhibits.title: Leah's 2025 data
exhibits.content:
- Modified AGI for the rental allowance: **$130,000**.
- Rental house she actively participates in managing: net loss **$30,000**.
- Limited partnership A (passive): net income **$8,000**.
- Limited partnership B (passive): net loss **$5,000**.
- She exercised incentive stock options with a bargain element of **$50,000** and still holds the shares.
- No prior-year suspended losses.

rows.label: Net passive loss before the rental allowance
Rental real estate special allowance available
Passive loss suspended and carried forward
Regular taxable income from the ISO exercise
rows.explanation: Exercising ISOs creates no regular income: **0**.

rows.label: AMT adjustment from the ISO exercise
rows.explanation: The bargain element is an AMT adjustment: **50,000**.

rows.label: If Leah sells the rental house to an unrelated buyer in 2026 in a taxable sale, the suspended rental losses are:
options: Usable only against future passive income
rows.explanation: A complete taxable disposition to an unrelated party frees suspended losses (§469(g)).

rows.label: To reduce AMT from future ISO exercises, Leah should consider:
options: Exercising all remaining options in one year
Converting the ISOs to nonqualified options after exercise
rows.explanation: Spreading exercises keeps each year's AMT adjustment below the level that triggers AMT.

rows.label: If her MAGI rises to $150,000, the special allowance becomes:
rows.explanation: The allowance phases out completely at $150,000 of MAGI.
